I study how brain and muscle signals could inform the control of wearable robots that assist movement.

Research interests

Current research

How can robots interpret
intended movements?

My current work focuses on neural and motion signals, with wearable assistance as a longer-term application.

Ongoing research

Symbiosis

From movement intent
to wearable assistance.

Symbiosis is my ongoing research on co-embodied intelligence. I am designing approaches to combine neural signals, body movement and environmental information for assistive control. Simulation and closed-loop evaluation are planned next steps.

Discuss a Symbiosis study ↗
Sense

Multimodal intent understanding

I am designing ways to align EEG, EMG, gaze and motion recordings, and to assess when each signal is reliable enough to inform a decision.

Predict

Shared world models

I am exploring models that represent the user and robot together, and predict movement while accounting for intent and physical constraints.

Assist

Closed-loop augmentation

The next steps are to test assistance and feedback in simulation, then evaluate how the components work together in a closed loop.

Proposed collaboration

When does EEG add useful information for assistive control?

A starting point for discussion is an arm-movement task in simulation: compare EMG and motion-based intent estimates with estimates that also use EEG. The task, data and evaluation protocol would be agreed with collaborators.

This is a proposed study, not a completed experiment or a validated wearable system.

What I would contribute

Neural decoding models, multimodal data processing and a simulation-based evaluation, drawing on my EEG and EMG and MuJoCo research experience.

Where collaborators could contribute

EEG and EMG acquisition expertise, access to suitable research data, wearable hardware constraints, or experience designing movement experiments.

What we could evaluate

Intent estimation, response latency and unintended control outputs, including what happens when a signal becomes unreliable. The aim would be a reproducible comparison and a decision about whether hardware integration is justified.
